entities.summary:
Fátima is a civil parish in Ourém, Portugal, and a site of Marian apparitions that have captivated millions of pilgrims since 1917. The apparitions, which took place between May 13 and October 13, 1917, were witnessed by three shepherd children, Lúcia Santos, Francisco Marto, and Jacinta Marto. The apparitions are believed to have been a series of miracles that took place in the presence of the Virgin Mary, who is said to have requested that the children pray for world peace and an end to war. The site has since become a major pilgrimage destination, attracting millions of visitors each year. The legacy of the Fátima apparitions has had a lasting impact on the Catholic Church and the world at large, shaping the way that many people think about faith, spirituality, and the role of the Church in the modern world.

The Fátima apparitions were a pivotal moment in modern Catholic history, marking a turning point in the Church's relationship with the world. The apparitions were a response to the devastating losses of World War I, and they called on the faithful to pray for peace and an end to war. The site has since become a place of healing and hope, where millions of people have come to seek solace and comfort in times of crisis.

Today, the Fátima shrine is one of the most famous and revered pilgrimage sites in the world, attracting millions of visitors each year. The site has been recognized as a place of international cultural and spiritual significance, and it has been designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The apparitions of Fátima have had a lasting impact on the world, inspiring countless works of art, literature, and music. They have also been the subject of numerous books, films, and other works that have sought to capture the essence and significance of this pivotal moment in modern Catholic history.
